key_insight: Classical machine-learning models distinguished Ghanaian mobile money scam SMS from legitimate messages, with Naive Bayes and linear SVM achieving perfect held-out scores on a small corpus.
engineering_relevance: Lightweight text classifiers offer a potential route to carrier- or handset-level scam filtering in low-resource settings.
method: Normalise currency amounts, phone numbers, and USSD codes.
Encode SMS text using TF-IDF unigrams and bigrams.
Compare Multinomial Naive Bayes, linear SVM, and Random Forest.
evidence_signal: On 220 labelled messages across 18 subcategories, five-fold cross-validation yielded mean accuracies of 96.6%, 94.9%, and 92.0% for Naive Bayes, SVM, and Random Forest, respectively; Naive Bayes and SVM achieved 1.00 accuracy, F1, and AUC on a 20% held-out test set.
watch_item: Perfect held-out results on a small, template-based corpus may not generalise to naturalistic, multilingual messages or evolving scams.
paper_title: Machine Learning-Based Detection of Mobile Money Scan Messages in Ghana: A Comparative Evaluation of Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, and Randon Forest Classifiers
